title: Jesus’ rebuke of Peter. Part 2
scripture_text: ‘’From that time on Jesus began to explain to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, the chief priests and the teachers of the law, and that he must be killed and on the third day be raised to life. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him. “Never, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to you!”
devotional:
Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me; you do not have in mind the concerns of God, but merely human concerns.” Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me. For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will find it. What good will it be for someone to gain the whole world, yet forfeit their soul? Or what can anyone give in exchange for their soul? For the Son of Man is going to come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he will reward each person according to what they have done.’’

Jesus expressed his authority over Satan.

Then Jesus says to Peter 'Get behind me Satan.' Jesus' words are reminiscent of his response to Satan, 'Away with you, Satan.' Matthew (4:10), at the conclusion of the wilderness temptation. The difference is that Jesus commanded Satan to move away or depart (Greek: hupago), Aramaic idiom for 'get out of my sight,' while he commands Peter to move (hupago again) to his proper position behind Jesus. This is the disciple's proper place, behind the Master following Him.

Jesus deals with the source of Peter's wrong thinking about Satan.

The proper place for Satan is behind us, in the sense that he mustn't be the object of our attention. This does not mean that we ignore him our pretend that he doesn't exist.

Rather, it means that we him put him and all that he has done to our lives behind us so we can really pursue God. Jesus then informs Peter; 'You are a stumbling block to me.' The word for stumbling block is skandalon from which we get our English word scandal. In Greek culture the word was used to describe the trigger in the trap on -which the bait placed which springs the trap when it is touched by the animal, causing the trap to close. It was also used to describe a stone on a pathway on which people would trip.

Skandalon always denotes the enticement or occasion leading to conduct which brings with it the ruin of the person in question. Skandala are things which lead others to turn away from God's salvation and thus to come to ruin. (Matt. 18:7. Luke 17:1). Imagine how terrible it would be being a stumbling block or a trap to the life of Jesus?

'Get behind me right now.' In front of me you're Satan, my stumbling block, behind me, you're Peter, my disciple. I can't build my church on you if you're standing in my way. Get behind me, where followers belong, where the church belongs.' Lastly Jesus tells us why Peter is acting in such a way. 'You do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.'What Jesus says here really exposes what is going on in Peter's heart. Matthew uses the word (phroneo) for mind.

The word Phroneo comes from the root word Phren that means the inner chambers of your heart. The word has an emphasis on the underlying disposition or attitude. Jesus' harsh critique of Peter involves more than just the few words he spoke on this occasion, but his inner attitude, the disposition of his heart, or we might even say, his very nature.

The word also has the sense of 'taking sides', 'supporting the cause of someone' e.g. when Josephus recounts the story of David's struggle to become king and the action of Abner, the commander of the opposing forces, seeking a political settlement with David. (2 Samuel 3) He says that the elders of Israel 'changed over to David's side' (Josephus. Antiquities 7.28). Mark uses this same idiom (8:33) to describe Peter's action. So Jesus is accusing Peter of shifting his loyalties and pursuing Satans agenda.

No matter how many Revelations a person may have received from God, from time to time they will need to experience the confrontation of Jesus.

We all have the potential to be instruments in the hand of Satan, and sometimes the only way we can be delivered from his influence is through a harsh confrontation with Jesus.

The influence of Satan is often appealing, he does not want you to suffer, especially for the sake of others.

God loves us the way we are, but he loves us too much to let us stay that way.

Peter would have never had become the rock if Jesus hadn't confronted him. Not allowing Jesus to transform our minds, can be the biggest threat to the Kingdom of God.
prayer: Father may your confrontation of me transform how I think and how I understand life.
